title: 客至
author: 杜甫
intro: A rare visitor comes to Du Fu's riverside cottage. The path hasn't been swept in ages, the food is plain and the wine is cloudy — so he calls the old neighbour over the fence to finish the cups with them. Warm, funny and very human.
analysis: 这首诗写杜甫在成都草堂招待客人。第一、二句写草堂的环境：房前房后都是春天的江水，只看见一群群鸥鸟天天飞来。鸥鸟常来，说明这里很安静，也暗示平时没有什么客人。第三、四句是有名的对句：长满花的小路，从来没有因为有客人来而打扫过；简陋的柴门，今天第一次为您打开。这两句写出主人见到客人的惊喜和真诚。第五、六句写招待：离集市太远，盘子里的菜只有一样；家里穷，杯里只有自家酿的旧酒。主人一边道歉，一边热情，很亲切。最后两句最有意思：您愿意和隔壁的老人一起喝吗？我隔着篱笆喊他过来，把剩下的酒都喝完！整首诗像一段家常话，写出了乡村生活的淳朴（朴实、真诚）和朋友之间的温暖。
analysisEn: Here Du Fu is entertaining a guest at his thatched cottage in Chengdu. The first couplet sets the scene: spring water all around the house, north and south, and nothing to see but flocks of gulls that come day after day. The gulls hint at how quiet it is — and at how seldom anyone visits. The second couplet is often quoted: the flower-lined path has never been swept for a guest; the rough wicker gate opens today, for the first time, for you. You can feel the host's delight and slight embarrassment. The third couplet is about the meal. The market is far, so there's only one dish on the plate; the family is poor, so the wine in the jar is old home-brew. He apologises and fusses, like any host. Then the ending: would you mind drinking with the old man next door? I'll call him over the hedge, and we'll finish off what's left. The whole poem reads like friendly conversation, full of the simple warmth of country life and friendship.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this around 761 at his thatched cottage in Chengdu. A note under the original title says the guest was a Mr Cui, a county magistrate; tradition says he was a relative on Du Fu's mother's side.
pronunciation: 舍南舍北 shè（房舍，不读 shě）；为君开 wèi；盘飧 sūn（生僻字，熟食、饭菜）；樽 zūn；旧醅 pēi（生僻字，未过滤的酒）；相对饮 xiāng；余杯 yú。
version: 采用通行教材版本。原题下有杜甫自注“喜崔明府相过”。“樽酒”有的版本作“尊酒”，“尊”是“樽”的古字。

lines.py: shè nán shè běi jiē chūn shuǐ
lines.lit: South of the house, north of the house, all spring water;
lines.en: Spring water all around my cottage, north and south,

lines.py: dàn jiàn qún ōu rì rì lái
lines.lit: I only see flocks of gulls come day after day.
lines.en: and all I see are the gulls that come each day.

lines.py: huā jìng bù céng yuán kè sǎo
lines.lit: The flower path has never been swept because of a guest;
lines.en: The flowery path has never been swept for a visitor;

lines.py: péng mén jīn shǐ wèi jūn kāi
lines.lit: the thatched gate today for the first time opens for you.
lines.en: today my rough gate opens for the first time — for you.

lines.py: pán sūn shì yuǎn wú jiān wèi
lines.lit: Food on the plate: the market far, no second flavour;
lines.en: The market's far, so there's just one dish on the table;

lines.py: zūn jiǔ jiā pín zhǐ jiù pēi
lines.lit: wine in the jar: the house poor, only old unstrained brew.
lines.en: we're poor, so the wine is only old home-brew.

lines.py: kěn yǔ lín wēng xiāng duì yǐn
lines.lit: Are you willing to drink face to face with the old neighbour?
lines.en: Would you share a drink with the old man next door?

lines.py: gé lí hū qǔ jìn yú bēi
lines.lit: Across the hedge I'll call him to finish the remaining cups.
lines.en: I'll call him over the hedge, and we'll empty every cup.

words.note: “至”是到；现代汉语有“至今”“宾至如归”。
现代汉语有“宿舍”“校舍”。读 shè，不读“舍不得”的 shě。
“但”古义是“只”，现代汉语“但”多是“但是”；成语“但愿”还保留古义。
“径”是小路，现代汉语有“小径”“途径”。

words.en: because of; for the sake of
words.note: 古义是“因为”；现代汉语有“缘故”“缘由”。
用蓬草编的门，指穷人家；现代汉语还有谦辞“蓬荜生辉”。
“飧”是熟食、饭菜，生僻字，现代汉语不用。
“兼”是同时有两样以上，现代汉语有“兼职”“兼顾”。
古代盛酒的器具，现代汉语里不常用。
“醅”是没有过滤的酒，生僻字。古人以新酒为贵，“旧醅”是谦虚的说法。
现代汉语也说，如“他不肯来”。
“翁”是老人，现代汉语有“渔翁”“老翁”，比较书面。
“余”是剩下的，现代汉语有“剩余”“多余”。

imagery.name: 鸥
imagery.zh: 鸥鸟天天来，写出草堂的幽静，也暗示平时只有鸟、没有客人，和下文“客至”的惊喜相呼应。
imagery.en: Gulls come daily — a sign of how quiet the cottage is, and that birds are usually its only visitors, which makes the guest's arrival a real event.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 房前房后的春水，写出草堂环境的清幽和与世隔绝。
imagery.en: Spring water all around shows how secluded and peaceful the cottage is.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 自家的旧酒虽然简陋，却是主人最真诚的招待，最后连邻居也叫来同喝。
imagery.en: The old home-brew is humble, but it is offered with total sincerity — and even the neighbour is called in to share it.
